questions.q: What two deployable artifacts does the northfield-data-platform repo version-control and deploy?
options: The Glue ETL job's PySpark script and the Step Functions state machine's ASL definition
The Redshift table DDL and the Athena workgroup configuration only
IAM policy documents only
The CloudWatch dashboard JSON only
questions.explain: The repo holds glue-jobs/northfield-orders-etl.py and state-machines/northfield-pipeline-orchestrator.asl.json, both deployed by the workflow.

questions.q: What triggers the GitHub Actions deploy workflow?
options: A push to main that touches files under glue-jobs/ or state-machines/
Any commit to any branch in the repo
A manual button click in the AWS console
A nightly cron schedule independent of code changes
questions.explain: The workflow's on: push trigger is scoped to main with a paths filter limiting it to glue-jobs/** and state-machines/** changes.

questions.q: Why does the workflow use OIDC to assume northfield-github-actions-deploy-role instead of storing an AWS access key in GitHub Secrets?
options: OIDC avoids any long-lived AWS credential sitting in GitHub, since the role is assumed only for the job's duration and the trust policy restricts which repo/branch can assume it
GitHub Secrets cannot store AWS credentials at all
OIDC is required by AWS for all S3 uploads
Stored access keys are faster to authenticate than OIDC
questions.explain: OIDC federation means no long-lived key is stored anywhere, and the role's trust policy scopes exactly which repo and branch may assume it.

questions.q: What does the trust policy's StringEquals condition on token.actions.githubusercontent.com:sub restrict?
options: Which exact repository and branch is allowed to assume the deploy role
Which AWS region the role can be used in
The maximum session duration for the assumed role
Which IAM users can view the role's permissions
questions.explain: The sub condition pins the trust to repo:northfield-org/northfield-data-platform:ref:refs/heads/main specifically, so even a fork's workflow can't assume the role.

questions.q: What does deploying the Glue script and state machine via CI/CD achieve that manual console edits don't?
options: Changes become reviewable, diffable pull requests instead of unreviewed direct edits that could be silently overwritten
It makes the Glue job run faster at execution time
It removes the need for the northfield-glue-role IAM policy
It automatically fixes bugs in the PySpark transformation logic
questions.explain: The lesson's core point is that version-controlled deploys make changes reviewable and prevent someone's console edit from being silently reverted by the next deploy.
